races.name: Oddschecker Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charlie Johnston with David Egan up; two wins at 8f on heavy ground but the step to 10f on good-to-firm is unproven — he sets the pace but his ability to sustain it over this trip on fast ground is the key question, and his STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is already stretching beyond his natural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Laureate Crown
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's progressive 3yo is on a sharp upward curve having won back-to-back at 8f, and Oisin Murphy's big-race craft is a clear asset; as the only true hold-up horse in the field he needs a genuine gallop to be set up for him, and a slow-run race on the Rowley Mile is his principal risk.

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's charge has won twice at 10f (good and standard) and holds solid place claims at the trip; Marco Ghiani has ridden him to good effect and his course-suitable profile as a genuine prominent type makes him well-suited to sitting just off Evanesco — the 38-day gap is the main watch point, but Botti's freshened horses often run well.

runners_data.name: Decade Of Time
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's lightly-raced improver arrives on a hat-trick bid having won his last two at 8f, and the step up to 10f on quicker ground is a logical next test; he is a natural front-runner or prominent racer by instinct but is mapped to midfield because the lead is already taken — his best chance depends on getting a clear run and finishing strongly despite his unnatural tactical position.

runners_data.name: Princling
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out this course-familiar 3yo who won over 8f at Goodwood on good ground with Tom Marquand, a pairing with a strong record; he is another true prominent type who will be inconvenienced by Evanesco's presence, needing to race further back than ideal, and his lack of a 10f win on the clock remains a query.

runners_data.name: Heraldry
runners_data.note: The John & Thady Gosden yard send out this interesting runner for William Buick — only three career starts but a course win and a Newmarket runner-up confirm he handles the track; 67 days off the track is notable, and while his natural style suits racing prominently, he is pushed into midfield by the congested front-running picture, meaning Buick's positioning skills become crucial.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate from the front at a controlled, honest pace on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f at Newmarket. With Evanesco able to set his own rhythm unchallenged, the tempo is likely to be measured rather than pressured, creating a rail-hugging, tactical contest that rewards those able to travel smoothly in behind and produce a sustained late kick on the Rowley Mile's stiff finish. Laureate Crown, the sole genuine hold-up horse, will be forced to close from the rear on a track that demands both tactical position and a quality finish. This race shape — an uncontested front-runner on good-to-firm ground over a galloping track — decisively favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce, rather than true hold-up horses needing a strong gallop to be set up for them. Note that Decade Of Time, Princling, and Heraldry are all natural prominent types but cannot all claim that position; Evanesco and Archers Bay are best placed to occupy the front ranks, with the trio of redistributed horses most likely shuffled into a midfield they would not naturally choose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evanesco Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco leads without pressure and sets a controlled pace that stretches the field on the run from halfway.
scenarios.body: Evanesco dictates the fractions from the front, keeps the pace honest but not brutal, and his rivals are forced to come around him in the straight; horses with a prominent gear and a genuine turn of foot thrive as the race becomes a two-furlong sprint from the two-pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a well-placed prominent type stalks Evanesco through the final bend and overwhelms him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: One of the chasing pack sits a length or two off the leader throughout, conserving energy while Evanesco does the donkey work, then quickens past in the final 100 yards; on good-to-firm Newmarket ground this is the most natural way for a quality 3yo to win from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves faster than expected, stretching the field and enabling Laureate Crown to close powerfully from the rear.
scenarios.body: Should the tempo quicken sufficiently to string the race out, Laureate Crown — with Oisin Murphy to orchestrate the run — can pick off tired rivals in the final furlong; his two recent wins and strong good-going form make him the one hold-up threat capable of exploiting a truly run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the entire field converges at the two-furlong pole and the result becomes a pure sprint lottery.
scenarios.body: With multiple natural prominent types forced into unnatural positions behind a single pace-setter, an unusually steady gallop could produce a bunched, scrimmaging finish; horses with the highest cruising speed and cleanest passage benefit most, but this scenario is structurally unlikely given Evanesco's front-running profile.

watchPoints.text: Archers Bay is 38 days fresh and Marco Botti's yard strikes at 2/19 over 14 days — watch closely in the market for stable confidence before post time, as a well-prepared prominent racer over a proven trip is the profile most suited to this pace map.

Laureate Crown's entire chance hinges on the tempo — if Evanesco dawdles in front, Murphy will have no pace to aim at and this hold-up horse may struggle to find the acceleration needed on a wide-open Rowley Mile straight.

Decade Of Time, Princling, and Heraldry are all natural front-runners or prominent types crammed into midfield; watch for crowding and interference as multiple horses attempt to improve their position entering the final two furlongs, which could compromise any or all three.

Good-to-firm ground at Newmarket puts a premium on horses with proven fast-ground form — Laureate Crown (good-to-firm winner), Archers Bay (good winner), and Princling (good winner) all hold relevant credentials, while Evanesco's two wins came on heavy ground, which is worth factoring into stamina assessments over 10f.

George Bass takes the ride on Decade Of Time for Jack Channon — an apprentice pairing in a competitive Heritage Handicap where tactical errors in a small, compact field could prove costly if the race is truly slowly run and positional judgement matters.

races.name: Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes (Sponsored By Ultimate Provence) (Fillies' Group 2)

runners_data.name: Acclamation Star
runners_data.note: Won on debut at 6f on Good but steps sharply up in class to Group 2 here; a natural front-runner by inclination, the sheer number of prominent types in this field means she is unlikely to get anywhere near her preferred early position, which compromises her chance meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Alwaysanangel
runners_data.note: Won her sole start at 6f on Good in Ireland for Joseph O'Brien, now supplemented into Group 2 company; Dylan Browne McMonagle has live Group-race form and she maps naturally to the prominent position she needs — no going concern, no headgear, only nine days since her last run which is sharp preparation.

runners_data.name: Etonnante
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's unbeaten juvenile won over this exact trip on Good ground, and Clifford Lee is a capable pilot; 43 days off is the one query, but Burke sends them fit and she is proven at the level — an ideal profile for a race where the front end is controlled and a short, sharp kick is what wins.

runners_data.name: Jolivette
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's filly won on her second start at 6f on Good for Colin Keane, but finished ninth on debut — the experience gap is modest; in truth a prominent-type racer, she is squeezed back by the traffic of runners ahead of her stylistically, making Keane's job more reactive than he would ideally want.

runners_data.name: Libertango
runners_data.note: Two wins from two starts over 6f on Good ground give Libertango the strongest form profile among those redistributed, and Boughey's yard is in reasonable nick; mapped toward the rear only because the prominent slots are saturated, she is genuinely the least out-of-role of the displaced runners — Billy Loughnane can ride a patient race if forced to.

runners_data.name: Ruby Moon
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, Richard and Peter Fahey's filly won her only start over 6f on Good and Ryan Moore immediately commits to riding her up front; uncontested lead on fast ground at Newmarket is a major asset, and Moore will not waste energy — the key question is whether her form is Group 2 class.

runners_data.name: Senorita Bonita
runners_data.note: Simon and Ed Crisford's filly won over 5f before finishing runner-up, and Oisin Murphy's class is obvious; she wants to be in the firing line from early but the congestion of prominent types will see her forced to race in a more patient manner, and she also faces a 1f trip extension into Group 2 company simultaneously.

runners_data.name: Troublesome Guest
runners_data.note: Ran 13th then 3rd in her two starts on Good over 6f, giving her an unknown tactical profile flagged by the ⚠ marker; David Egan takes the ride for a small trainer (0 wins from 5 in 14 days), and the form is too inconsistent to read confidently — she is the wildcard of the field.

races.paceDynamic: Ruby Moon is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with Ryan Moore aboard, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — this is not a race where she will be pressured into going suicidally fast. The field is heavily stacked with prominent-running types: Alwaysanangel, Etonnante, Acclamation Star, Jolivette, and Senorita Bonita all want to race prominently, meaning several will be forced to sit off their natural position and race in a more restrained manner than they would prefer. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Ruby Moon is best placed to secure the rail and dictate, with Alwaysanangel and Etonnante (both OR 120, both proven over 6f on Good) most likely to actually lock in the early prominent slots behind her, while Jolivette, Acclamation Star and Senorita Bonita will be shuffled back against their will. A steady-to-moderate pace set by a single uncontested leader over 6f on Good to Firm at Newmarket heavily favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken in the final two furlongs — the high-class prominent types with proven form over this course and trip hold a decisive positional edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ruby Moon Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ruby Moon dictates an uncontested, controlled pace and the prominent chasers lack the acceleration to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Moore settles Ruby Moon into an easy rhythm, denying any rival an obvious target, and she simply finds enough in the final furlong on a sound surface that suits her form profile. Horses who can travel close to the pace — Alwaysanangel and Etonnante — are best positioned to challenge but may find her too good if she has conserved her energy perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ruby Moon's early fractions are just quick enough to set up a strong finishing effort from the chasers immediately behind her.
scenarios.body: Alwaysanangel and Etonnante, both OR 120 with proven winning form over 6f on Good ground, travel in the slipstream and produce the sharper turn of foot in the final furlong to overhaul the leader. Good to Firm Newmarket suits both, and with top jockeys aboard neither will be caught flat-footed when the race quickens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistibuted Type Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a repositioned prominent runner — most likely Senorita Bonita with Oisin Murphy — finds cleaner air from an unfamiliar midfield berth and runs on strongly.
scenarios.body: Murphy's horsemanship could transform Senorita Bonita's enforced midfield position into a tactical advantage, tracking cover and finishing with momentum if the pace is truly even. However, this scenario depends on a horse racing out of its natural role, which structurally reduces its probability, and Senorita Bonita steps up in class from 5f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Troublesome Guest Outrun Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Troublesome Guest, despite her inconsistent form (13th then 3rd), bounces back to her best and the field finishes in a heap.
scenarios.body: Troublesome Guest's unknown style profile introduces genuine uncertainty, and if the race develops chaotically with the overloaded prominent group interfering with each other she could sneak a place at a price. This is a low-probability, chaos-dependent outcome relying on structural disorder that a Ryan Moore-led race is unlikely to produce.

watchPoints.text: Ruby Moon (Moore) — watch for her jumping straight to the front from the gate; if she gets a clean lead with no immediate challenge from Alwaysanangel or Etonnante by the 3f pole, the race may already be over.

Alwaysanangel and Etonnante — both OR 120 prominent types will contest the same early tracking position behind Ruby Moon; watch for interference or bumping in the first furlong as they fight for the rail slot.

Jolivette and Acclamation Star — both natural front-runners expected to be shuffled back involuntarily; if either over-races fighting for position in the first two furlongs, their finishing effort will be materially compromised.

Libertango (Loughnane/Boughey) — mapped to hold-up but is a genuine two-from-two winner over this trip; if Loughnane accepts the rear early and times his run wide into the final furlong, she offers value relative to her redistribution tag.

Troublesome Guest — her unknown style means watch the early stages to identify whether Egan sends her forward or sits quietly; her final position will tell you more than her form figures do about whether she belongs in this company.

races.name: Betway Trophy (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Roaring Legend
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field; Colin Keane will find himself with a completely uncontested lead, which is a major tactical asset, but his OR of 103 means he is weighted to his ceiling and his similar-going form reads just 0W0P from 5 runs, which is a concern for the win even if he controls proceedings.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Consistent horse with two wins and three places on similar going from six runs, and the 1m6f trip is well within range, but a finishing position of 8th over 2m0f on Good last time is a flag — William Buick's stable companion Valedictory may actually suit this shape better; twin-trainer situation with Ian Williams worth noting.

runners_data.name: Real Dream
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist whose similar-going record reads 0W3P from 12 runs — fine at placing but struggles to convert — and his last six efforts include a run of 13th, 7th, 7th, 13th which suggests he needs everything to fall perfectly; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is a marginal offset at best.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for the powerful Gosden yard on a lightly-raced four-year-old who has won twice at 1m4f and shown strong Good-ground form (1W3P from 5 similar-going runs); the step up to 1m6f is an open question but his profile screams a horse who will travel prominently and quicken.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f on Good ground 40 days ago and arrives in form, with David Egan booked for Dylan Cunha; his best efforts have come at shorter than today's 1m6f and his recent 12th over this exact trip on Tapeta is not ignored, but his prominent style means he will be ideally placed tactically.

runners_data.name: Goblet Of Fire
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's raider has won twice over 1m4f–1m6f and carries live form (/21-51), but a 68-day absence and Saffie Osborne's booking for a yard that is 0/5 in the last fortnight are slight negatives; as a natural prominent type bumped back to midfield on this map, he will likely push forward regardless, making his true map position closer to Scenario A territory.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse who finished second over 1m2f on Good at Goodwood 13 days ago — genuine recent form — but all five historical runs in the dataset were over shorter trips than today's 1m6f, and his best finishing position in this data is 2nd, suggesting he needs a true pace to come from off it.

runners_data.name: Wine Dark Sea
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's four-year-old is in sparkling form with three wins in his last five including back-to-back victories, all prominently ridden; he is a genuine front-runner displaced to midfield on this map because of the traffic jam at the front, and Lewis Edmunds will almost certainly try to push forward — the style mismatch is real and his OR of 83 also sets a task.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' hold-up type has a modest recent form string of 008-78 and his similar-going record of 1W4P from 9 runs is uninspiring at this level; he needs a strongly-run race and a clear passage, neither of which is guaranteed given Roaring Legend's lone-leader setup.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's consistent handler has saddled 9/67 in 14 days suggesting a yard in form, but Pole Star's own form reads 0-4350 with an 11th on Soft last time; a natural prominent type redistributed to midfield, Connor Beasley will look to push forward, but OR 86 off a career-best effort looks stretched at this level on quick ground.

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Legend is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no credible challenger for the lead over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket — he will bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo with Colin Keane able to dictate the fractions entirely on his own terms. Behind him, Beylerbeyi, Valedictory, and Asgard's Captain are the natural prominent horses most likely to sit in second, third, and fourth, whilst Goblet Of Fire, Wine Dark Sea, and Pole Star — all genuine prominent types — cannot all find their preferred berth and at least two of them will be shuffled back into a midfield or hold-up role they do not naturally want; of the three, Goblet Of Fire's course-and-distance form gives it the best chance of pressing forward, with Pole Star next, and Wine Dark Sea likely to be the one most inconvenienced. With a lone, uncontested pace-setter controlling a truly run 1m6f trip on quick ground, the race sets up strongly for horses that can sit close to the action and sustain their effort through the straight — prominent racers with proven stamina and tactical flexibility are the primary beneficiaries, whilst genuine hold-up horses face a stern test of whether there is enough pace for them to pounce from off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Reward
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend dictates an unchallenged, even gallop and the race is truly run from the front.
scenarios.body: Roaring Legend sets a sustainable fractions that rewards horses travelling prominently behind him, with the straight at Newmarket exposing those who lack stamina or cannot sustain a run from a close-up position; the winner is most likely to be a horse that has sat second or third and picked off the leader inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend's pace is slow enough to leave him with a devastating turn of foot and no rival can reel him in.
scenarios.body: Keane times his move to perfection, the field chases fruitlessly up the Newmarket straight, and Roaring Legend's stamina at this trip proves superior to anything behind; the prominent chasers do not accelerate sharply enough to close the deficit in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely testing and a hold-up horse finds a clear passage to run through beaten rivals late.
scenarios.body: Majestic or Wine Dark Sea — both capable of finishing strongly from off the pace — benefit if the leaders tie each other up in a contested run home; however, with Roaring Legend uncontested and several redistributed prominent types not truly comfortable sitting deep, this scenario requires a pace collapse that the race shape makes unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Legend sets a falsely slow gallop that collapses into a sprint finish, negating stamina entirely.
scenarios.body: A messy tactical race with no true pace sees the field bunch and the final two furlongs become a flat-out dash, favouring sharp finishers over stayers; the redistribution of several prominent types into unnatural positions could cause positional scrimmaging that further disrupts rhythm for hold-up horses.

watchPoints.text: Valedictory (William Buick, Gosden) has the profile — prominent style, Good-ground form, improving four-year-old — to sit second or third off Roaring Legend's uncontested lead and deliver a sustained challenge up the straight; watch if he travels smoothly past halfway.

Goblet Of Fire, Wine Dark Sea, and Pole Star are all natural prominent types mapped to midfield — if two or more push forward early to claim a tracking position, a positional bunching behind Roaring Legend could cause scrimmaging and compromise several horses' rhythm in the first half of the race.

Roaring Legend's uncontested lead is a double-edged sword — Keane could set a falsely slow gallop that leaves him with reserves in the tank, converting a handicap into a near-sprint off a slow early pace; watch the opening half-mile splits to gauge whether the pace is truly genuine.

Asgard's Captain won over 1m2f on Good ground recently but today's 1m6f is the longest trip in the dataset for this horse — watch his position at the 3f pole to see if he is still travelling or already under pressure, which would be an early signal the stamina is found wanting.

Majestic is the hold-up horse with the most live recent form (2nd, 13 days ago) but relies on a truly-run race to deliver from off the pace — if Roaring Legend's tempo is pedestrian through the first mile, Tom Marquand will be sitting on a horse with nowhere to go and no pace to aim at.

races.name: Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Falmouth Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 1)

runners_data.name: Balantina
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien-trained three-year-old who ran a creditable second in a Group 2 on good ground over this trip last time; her style is genuinely prominent and she should hold a natural position here, but that Oaks fifth at Epsom raises the question of whether she truly belongs at this level in a straight-mile Group 1.

runners_data.name: Evolutionist
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has solid Group-race form at a mile on good ground, including a win and two thirds; she is a front-running type by nature but the congestion of prominent runners in this field means she is likely to be shuffled wider and further back than suits her, which tempers confidence in her chance.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners the A P O'Brien three-year-old who carries the best recent form in the race — four wins including back-to-back at a mile on good ground; as the lone confirmed pace-setter she gets a completely uncontested lead, and her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she is being shown in a front position that is genuinely her role, though the flag is a reminder that lone-leader races can be tricky if the pace is misjudged.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has placed twice at a mile on good ground but also has a soft-ground win at 12f, and while she is a front-running type, the depth of prominent competition here means she is unlikely to get that position and will need to produce an improved performance racing further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Venosa
runners_data.note: The second A P O'Brien runner is a hold-up type whose record over this trip on good ground is limited, and a 61-day absence combined with modest RPR (89) and no wins in seven career starts makes her a difficult proposition at Group 1 level regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Blue Bolt
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old carries a 9lb penalty as the older mare but her five wins at Newmarket's mile on good or good-to-firm ground make her the most course-and-distance-proven runner in the field; Colin Keane will ride her patiently from a prominent-to-midfield position and she must be respected wherever the race develops.

runners_data.name: Jancis
runners_data.note: The five-year-old trained by W McCreery has three wins at a mile on good ground and proven course form, but is a natural prominent racer whose chances are compromised by being forced further back than she prefers; Sean Levey will try to sit as close as possible, and her LR of 23 days is straightforward, but the style mismatch is a real factor in a race this short of an early cavalry charge.

races.paceDynamic: Precise (Ryan Moore, A P O'Brien) is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, she will dictate from the gates at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight mile. Blue Bolt and Balantina will press into prominent positions behind her, meaning the race will be run at a honest but not brutal gallop — enough to test stamina without producing a truly searching pace test that destroys front-runners. This field holds more prominent-minded types than the race shape can accommodate: Jancis, Evolutionist, and Venetian Lace are all natural prominent racers who will be unable to secure their preferred pitch and will be shuffled back into a midfield they don't naturally inhabit, compromising their chances. The resulting shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured pace with a tight, bunched chasing pack — strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles, particularly those proven at the trip on fast ground, as the absence of a punishing early burn means the leader's stamina reserves are preserved for a finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Precise Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Precise is allowed to stride on uncontested and quicken from two furlongs out before the pack can organise.
scenarios.body: Precise has already won four times on good ground over a mile and Ryan Moore will exploit the empty lead, building a rhythm that is hard to disrupt; without a rival willing to pressurise her at any stage, she will have enough left in the tank to repel all challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Blue Bolt Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to blunt Precise and Blue Bolt produces her trademark strong late run from a tracking position.
scenarios.body: Blue Bolt has five wins over this exact course-and-distance combination and her Good to Firm record of 5W from 6 is outstanding; Colin Keane will time the challenge to arrive late and with purpose, potentially catching Precise if she has gone too soon.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Overhauls Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Precise's solo lead produces a falsely slow early pace that sets up a sprint finish benefitting the closet chasers.
scenarios.body: Balantina and Evolutionist, tracking just behind the leader, would be best-positioned to pounce in a sprint-to-the-line scenario; however, Evolutionist is racing outside her natural role and Balantina's recent form includes a fifth in the Oaks, so reliability at this level is uncertain.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Emerges Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a crawl, a chaotic sprint finish develops and a hold-up type finds a gap to land a surprise blow.
scenarios.body: Venosa (A P O'Brien) is a remote chance on current form — her best Irish Flat figures are modest and her six starts include no win at this level — but chaos in a bunched finish occasionally surfaces a longshot; Jancis, despite being pushed out of her natural position, has placed twice at a mile on good ground and could also figure if everything breaks her way.

watchPoints.text: Precise (Moore/A P O'Brien) is entirely uncontested at the head of affairs — watch whether Moore elects to increase tempo after the two-furlong pole or conserve energy, as the decision will define the entire finish.

Blue Bolt carries a 9lb Group 1 penalty as the four-year-old in this field of three-year-olds — if that weight concession blunts her finishing effort on a flat-out Good to Firm surface, she may be swallowed up despite arriving in the best form of her career.

Jancis, Evolutionist, and Venetian Lace are all genuine front-runners forced into a midfield berth they don't naturally occupy — monitor how their jockeys manage positions in the early stages, as any one of them pushing forward could create unexpected pressure on Precise.

Venosa has been off for 61 days and has no wins in seven starts, but A P O'Brien often targets these fillies' Group 1s with unexposed types — watch the market move in the final hour for any late support that could signal stable confidence.

Going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race despite the header listing Good — all runners show good-to-firm going as OK, but note Venetian Lace has two soft-ground runs in her last five, so the faster surface is a mild positive point for the prominently-proven Good to Firm specialists like Blue Bolt and Precise.

races.name: Weatherbys Banking Group British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: Tatterstall
runners_data.note: Strong course-and-distance profile with two recent top-3 finishes on good ground over 5f, genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to be honest; Connor Beasley partners and the 15-day turnaround is fine given his form, but this measured gallop is his primary concern.

runners_data.name: Rosario
runners_data.note: William Buick in the saddle is a significant booking for Roger Teal's 5yo, who handles good ground well (12/15 in similar conditions) but has been below his best lately with no win in five; a true closer who needs competitors to tire in front of him.

runners_data.name: Twilight Calls
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the mount on this 8yo veteran who has won on this course at 5f on good ground — the visor is in effect and the form figure of 1 in recent starts confirms he can deliver when the conditions stack up; naturally holds up and needs to be produced late.

runners_data.name: Rapper's Delight
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Richard Spencer, carrying the visor and returning quickly after just 5 days — that freshness can suit a 5f sprinter, and his two 2nd-place finishes at this trip on good-ground variants suggest he handles the conditions; his ability to sit just off Our Cody is the key tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Never Just A Dream
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners this 6yo for T J Kent in fair recent form at 6f on soft and standard; a true hold-up horse whose natural inclination to race from the rear is compressed by the field dynamic into a midfield map position — at a drop to 5f and on quicker ground, his range of form looks limited.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee rides this 4yo for Mike Murphy, whose 14-day strike rate of 2/5 is notable; form figure of 1 in a recent 6f stakes is eye-catching, but his good-ground profile over 5f is poor (0W0P in 4 tries), and his natural style means he is unlikely to see a strong pace ahead of him — he maps further forward than he will actually race.

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey booking for Tom Clover's 6yo, and his 5f course record on good ground is genuinely strong (3W4P in 13 runs); a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by the field composition, meaning Murphy will need to find a path through rather than his preferred sweeping run from the back.

runners_data.name: Our Cody
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore for Richard Hughes (T14: 3/41) — the sole front-runner who will dictate terms unopposed, and his 5f form on good ground is consistent (8/10 in similar conditions); the style-fit flag reflects that a 3yo giving weight all around in a handicap from the front is not without risk, but Moore's pace-judging ability is the key asset.

runners_data.name: Emperor Spirit
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides this 8yo for Michael Keady — has shown a tendency to fade in the finish which is a concern in a truly run race; the tongue-tie is in use and he has placed twice on good ground over 5f, but his true hold-up style means he is squeezed into a position on the map that doesn't reflect where he will actually be at halfway.

runners_data.name: Underwriter
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 3yo ridden by apprentice Kyle McHugh (7lb claim), which partially offsets a weight concern; his going form on good ground is solid (6/7), but recent form figures include an 8th and has shown a tendency to fade — likely to be held up and find this tempo insufficiently strong to produce his best.

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners Robert Cowell's 6yo, who is a genuine prominent racer in the correct map position; p headgear in use, good-ground form is respectable (7/15), and three places from five at 5f on good or similar going shows he handles conditions — ideally placed to stalk Our Cody.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Lemos De Souza's 3yo ridden by Connor Planas, carrying the lowest weight in the field at 121lbs — prominent style and good-to-firm course form exists in the hist, but strike rate on similar ground (0W1P) and trainer with no 14-day winner is a concern; the light weight is the one intriguing angle in an otherwise challenging profile.

races.paceDynamic: Our Cody is the sole confirmed front-runner here, ridden by Ryan Moore and likely to stride straight to the front from the gates, setting a sustainable and uncontested gallop over this straight Newmarket 5f on good-to-firm ground. With no natural rival for the early lead, the pace will be honest but not frenetic, meaning the first half of the race is likely run at a measured tempo that leaves Our Cody with energy in reserve entering the rising ground to the Rowley Mile finish. Tatterstall, Rosario, Twilight Calls, and Rocking Ends are the genuine hold-up types seeking to close from the rear, but their effectiveness is contingent on Our Cody either going too hard or finding a flat spot — unlikely given Moore's pedigree for front-running judgement. Star Chorus, Rocking Ends, Never Just A Dream, and Emperor Spirit have been redistributed into midfield on the map because the field holds more natural hold-up horses than can all realistically settle at the back in a 12-runner 5f sprint, but their true style means they will not be on the girth of Our Cody when it counts. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those who can stalk the controlled pace — horses who can sit just behind Our Cody in the first two furlongs and pick up efficiently on the rising ground, rather than true closers who need a searching gallop to drag them into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Our Cody gets a clean break and Moore dictates a sustainable tempo that saps the closing power of the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Our Cody sets fractions that are honest but never suicidal, allowing any prominent stalker — particularly Rapper's Delight or Rhythm N Hooves — to sit close and challenge, while the genuine closers from deep find insufficient gap to bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Our Cody sets a slightly stronger-than-expected pace, opening the door for those sitting just off the pace to arrive with a decisive run.
scenarios.body: Rapper's Delight or Rhythm N Hooves, positioned one to two lengths off the leader, find a clear passage on the rising ground and sustain their run to the line as Our Cody's advantage narrows; the slight early pressure is just enough to bring the mid-division types into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens early and the redistribution holds — meaning the natural hold-up horses actually do settle back — creating a fast-run race that draws the closers into play.
scenarios.body: Tatterstall and Rosario, both with strong going form on similar surfaces, have the finishing speed to close if given a true target; Twilight Calls, a course winner and dual 5f scorer on good ground, has the profile to nail a tiring favourite late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Pace, Chaos Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If there is early crowding or a faster-than-expected break that scrambles positions among the prominent types, producing a more ragged contest.
scenarios.body: U S S Charleston or Underwriter, both able to travel prominently at a reasonable price, could benefit from a stop-start rhythm that negates the pace advantage of Our Cody and rewards tactical adaptability over pure running style.

watchPoints.text: Our Cody (Ryan Moore) is the only genuine front-runner — watch whether Moore elects to go hard or conserve, as that single decision shapes the entire race outcome.

Rocking Ends (Oisin Murphy) is a strong-form closer on this course and trip in similar going, but will face a traffic challenge having been mapped into midfield rather than his natural rear position — watch for Murphy finding a gap on the outside from the 2f pole.

Star Chorus and Never Just A Dream both have style-fit flags and are true hold-up horses compressed into midfield on the map — if neither can get to their natural position, they are effectively out of the race before it begins.

Twilight Calls (Saffie Osborne) is a course-and-distance winner with the visor on who has placed on this ground twice in the last five runs — monitor whether she can find clear daylight to mount a late challenge from her hold-up position.

Rapper's Delight, returning after just 5 days with a prominent style and visor, is well-placed to sit directly behind Our Cody — any sign of a stumble or slow break from him would allow the hold-up horses to close the gap considerably.

races.name: Jockey Club Estates Handicap

runners_data.name: Flight Control
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on good ground at 3yo level, runs prominently and handles this going well — 4/4 on similar ground suggests she is well-suited by conditions, and a fresh 20-day break for William Pyle looks straightforward.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over on a horse who has form over this trip and won at 7f — naturally wants to be prominent but the race shape means he is likely to find himself in a more midfield berth than suits his best racing, which is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Calling A Star
runners_data.note: William Buick is a significant booking for Richard Hughes and this horse has two wins over 6-7f on good ground — by instinct a front-rank racer, but the congested pace scenario means he may not get the clean early position he needs, tempering his headline chance.

runners_data.name: Toastmaster
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy adds class in the saddle and Toastmaster has shown consistent form, winning over 7f on good recently — he naturally wants to be up there, and if Murphy conjures him a slot just off the pace he is the type to grind out a solid finish.

runners_data.name: Kimbara
runners_data.note: Consistent horse with multiple placed efforts over 7f on good ground and Richard Spencer has live form at T14 (5/19) — wants to race prominently and has the profile to hit the frame, but it all depends on whether George Wood can find her the right pitch in a congested early order.

runners_data.name: Lion of Mali
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's horse has a strong record of winning at 7f on good going (two wins in last 5, and a high hit-rate on this surface) — naturally prominent and David Egan will look to slot him in close to the pace, where his record suggests he is most dangerous.

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type, Gina Mangan's Irish raider needs a strong pace to deliver late — has a win over a longer trip on good ground and the form string shows consistency, but on a flat Newmarket 7f with a controlled pace, this style is at a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride on this hold-up filly for a trainer (Spencer, T14 6/18) who has been busy — the form shows mainly placed efforts at 6-8f in softer ground and the step back to good-to-firm over 7f is not obviously ideal, making a big performance from the rear hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Three Non Blondes
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani's mount is the one horse most likely to lead from the front — won at 7f on standard going and finished second on good, so ground is fine — she will set the terms of this race and a genuinely steady pace plays to her stamina-based style, though she is style-fit tagged against a big field.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the joint-top-rated runner for Ed Dunlop and Sierra Sands has two wins over 6-7f on good ground, with the most recent form strong — a prominent, racing-keenly type who Moore will slot in close to Three Non Blondes, and the profile fits this race shape as well as any runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Angel Gabriel
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is lightly raced, rated 81, and Edward Greatrex has the booking — ran 4th last time in a 6f handicap and is stepping up to 7f for the first time, which could be the key to unlocking improvement, though the lack of 7f or good-going form in the last four runs introduces some uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Three Non Blondes is the one confirmed front-runner and, on good-to-firm ground over 7f at Newmarket, she is likely to dictate at a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a scorching pace — her style-fit tag acknowledges she races out of her natural role here but she is still the clearest pace-setter in the field. The field is packed with horses whose natural instinct is to race prominently — Aqua Bear, Calling A Star, Toastmaster, Kimbara, and Lion of Mali are all genuine prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is not room for all of them to operate up with the pace. Of those, Sierra Sands and Angel Gabriel, who carry the highest ORs alongside Three Non Blondes and have genuine early pace, are the most likely to actually secure prominent positions behind the leader. A controlled, single-paced gallop set by Three Non Blondes, with a bunched midfield group tracking in behind, strongly favours horses who can race in the first three or four and sustain their effort through the dip — prominent racers and those with a high cruising speed are at a premium; true hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Three Non Blondes sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race develops into a sustained, even-tempo affair from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Three Non Blondes dictates at her own pace and the winner will emerge from the small group that tracks her closest throughout; Sierra Sands and Angel Gabriel, the highest-rated horses likely to hold a prominent pitch, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group creates unexpected early pressure that finds Three Non Blondes out and the tempo lifts significantly.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early pace burns off the pace-setters and opens the door for those sitting just behind the lead to swoop through in the final 2f; horses like Toastmaster and Lion of Mali, who were pushed back on the map but are naturally prominent, benefit if they find a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle mile to leave the closers with ground to make up at a realistic tempo.
scenarios.body: Daretobedifferent has course-and-distance form and enough stamina for 7f, and would benefit from any strung-out finish; Ice Cube needs everything to go right from the rear but has occasional ability to hit the frame.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Kimbara or Aqua Bear Slot In
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types successfully claims a front-rank position and the pace stays honest enough to reward a stalking run.
scenarios.body: Kimbara has a solid recent record over 7f on good ground at this level and if she gets her natural racing position she has the profile to finish strongly; Aqua Bear has won at this trip and style, and a smooth passage from a prominent berth would maximise his chance.

watchPoints.text: Sierra Sands — Ryan Moore on the joint-top-rated horse who has two wins at this trip on good ground; if he slots in just behind Three Non Blondes, this combination of jockey, pace and profile makes him the most dangerous runner if the race unfolds cleanly.

Prominent-group congestion — Aqua Bear, Calling A Star, Toastmaster, Kimbara and Lion of Mali all want to be up close to Three Non Blondes, creating a genuine risk of early barging and jostling that could unsettle several of them and compromise their chances.

Lion of Mali — James Fanshawe's horse has an excellent record winning at 7f on good, and if David Egan manoeuvres him into a prominent position from his drawn stall, his track record suggests he could easily outrun his odds.

Three Non Blondes — watch her early speed from the gate; if she is allowed a clear lead without being pressured, she sets the entire tactical shape of the race, but if she is immediately challenged by one of the other prominent types the tempo could rise sharply and change the complexion entirely.

Daretobedifferent — the only true closer in the field alongside Ice Cube; if the controlled pace predicted here materialises, watch whether she can pick up late at all, as it will signal whether there is any residual pace deficit for the leaders to exploit.
